close_reason: Landed in commit c77e28c. handle_space_get now parses /get properties argument (previously ignored) and applies the bd:JMAP-v9py.4 non-member field-projection trim: member or anonymous (single-user) callers see full Space with properties filter honored; non-members of an isPubliclyPreviewable=true Space see the 8-field restricted view, intersected with properties as a hard cap; non-members of an isPubliclyPreviewable=false Space currently fall through unchanged (TODO marker for bd:JMAP-v9py.20). 7 tests in tests/space_get_projection.rs cover all four branches plus the TODO marker.
description:
Spec source: draft-atwood-jmap-chat-00 §Space/get (after JMAP-v9py.19 lands).

## Background

This bead was originally written to target `handle_space_query` and to perform a field-projection trim on /query response objects. The implementing agent (do-beads session, 2026-05-13) found two problems:

1. The bead's premise was factually wrong about the current code: `handle_space_query` in `crate-jmap-chat-server/src/space.rs:319-325` already returns the RFC 8620 §5.5 standard shape (only `ids`). There were no "fields" to trim.

2. The spec text on line 1182 of draft-atwood-jmap-chat-00 conflated /query (which returns ids per §5.5) and /get (which returns objects + applies the `properties` filter per §5.1). Implementing the bead literally would have forced a non-standard objects-bearing response field on /query.

Decision (Mark, 2026-05-13): pick Option B from the agent triage — split the rule cleanly. Discovery stays on `Space/query` (which ids non-members may see); field-trim moves to `Space/get` (which fields non-members receive). This matches the JMAP idiom used everywhere else (`Foo/query → #ids → Foo/get`).

The matching spec edit is tracked by JMAP-v9py.19 (this bead is now blocked by it). The companion notFound enforcement is split into JMAP-v9py.20.

## Acceptance

- `handle_space_get` in `crate-jmap-chat-server/src/space.rs` performs a non-member field-projection trim:
  * When caller is a member of the requested Space → return the full Space object subject to the standard JMAP `/get` `properties` filter (existing behavior, regression guard).
  * When caller is NOT a member of the requested Space AND `isPubliclyPreviewable: true` → return a restricted view containing ONLY the fields `id`, `name`, `description`, `iconBlobId`, `memberCount`, `createdAt`, `isPublic`, `isPubliclyPreviewable`. All other fields MUST be omitted from the returned object, even if explicitly requested via `properties`. The Space id MUST appear in `list`, MUST NOT appear in `notFound`.
- The non-member-vs-non-previewable case (caller not a member AND `isPubliclyPreviewable: false`) is left as a TODO marker in this bead's code drop, to be filled by JMAP-v9py.20. The TODO MUST be clearly commented so the follow-up bead's claimant lands on the right path.
- `handle_space_query` is unchanged from its current RFC 8620 §5.5 shape. The discovery rule (which ids non-members may see when filtering `isPublic: true`) is implementation-level work that already lives in the backend's query path; no handler change is required for that surface — the backend already filters based on caller-membership when applying the filter.

## Test plan

Tests live in `crate-jmap-chat-server/tests/` using the `MemoryBackend` + a `TestCallerCtx` pattern that returns a caller principal id. (The `TestCallerCtx` plumbing is in scope of this bead — it's been blocked on the JMAP-v9py.4 architectural decision; it lands here.)

- Member caller, /get of a fully-populated Space → response carries the full Space object (all spec fields present); the `properties` filter is honored if present. Regression guard.
- Non-member caller, /get of a Space with `isPubliclyPreviewable: true` → response carries the Space in `list` with only the 8 allowed fields; no other fields present even when caller passes `properties: ["roles", "members", ...]`. The id is NOT in `notFound`.
- Non-member caller, /get with `properties: ["id", "roles"]` of a Space with `isPubliclyPreviewable: true` → response includes `id` (in the allowed set) and OMITS `roles` (outside the allowed set), even though the caller asked for it. Sanity-check the projection is a hard cap, not a min.

## Out of scope

- The notFound classification for non-previewable Spaces (split to JMAP-v9py.20; blocked by JMAP-v9py.19).
- Caching membership decisions across multiple ids in a single /get call (deployment optimization, not normative).
- Changing the backend trait shape — `principal_id` already exists per the foundation-seam decision (JMAP-ga0q); the handler uses it directly.

## Blocked on

JMAP-v9py.19 (the matching spec edit must land first; until then the handler would diverge from the published spec).
title: Layer A: Space/get non-member field projection (isPubliclyPreviewable restricted view)
